questions.q: Why must retrieval and generation be measured separately when evaluating a RAG system?
options: Because they run on different servers and the metrics cannot be combined

Because the two halves fail independently — a faithful answer on wrong chunks is a retrieval failure, a hallucination on right chunks is a generation failure — and conflating them sends you tuning the wrong half
Because generation metrics are always higher than retrieval metrics
Because SQL Server can only store one kind of metric per table
questions.explain: The chapter stresses the two halves fail independently and are fixed independently; mixing their metrics up leads to tuning the wrong half of the pipeline.

questions.q: What does recall@k measure, and what makes it the headline retrieval metric?
options: How many chunks the reranker scores per millisecond
The fraction of answers the LLM refused to generate
Average latency of the top-k queries per second
The fraction of questions where at least one gold chunk appears in the top-k retrieved
questions.explain: Recall@k is the fraction of questions where at least one gold chunk appears in the top-k retrieved — the headline retrieval metric, computed against a labeled eval set of 100+ questions with known gold chunk IDs.

questions.q: What does 'faithfulness' mean as a generation metric, and what counts as a hallucination?
options: Whether the answer is written in fluent English
Whether every claim in the answer is supported by the retrieved context — a single unsupported claim is a hallucination
Whether the answer cites exactly three chunks
Whether the LLM answered within 2 seconds
questions.explain: Faithfulness decomposes the answer into atomic claims and verifies each against the retrieved chunks; a single unsupported claim is a hallucination.

questions.q: How should the eval rubric score a refusal ('I don't have information about that') when the context genuinely lacks the answer?
options: As a failure, because the pipeline should always answer
As partially correct, because the LLM attempted something
As correct behavior, not failure — otherwise the metrics punish honesty and reward hallucination
Refusals should be excluded from the eval set entirely
questions.explain: The chapter warns: score refusals as correct when the context genuinely lacks the answer, or your metrics will punish honesty and reward hallucination.

questions.q: What production online signal indicates the corpus is drifting away from user questions?
options: A rising median top-1 retrieval distance per query
A falling LLM token-per-second rate
An increasing DiskANN index file size
A rising number of SQL Server Agent jobs
questions.explain: Retrieval telemetry should log top-1 distance per query: a rising median distance means the corpus is drifting away from the questions — new topics, new vocabulary, stale chunks.
